01

Cameras see the grasp. They can't feel it.

The challenge

Robot learning runs on video and joint angles. But manipulation succeeds or fails at the contact patch — how hard each finger presses, where the load sits, when an object starts to slip. A camera sees none of it. SensePoint records that missing channel, in sync with the demonstration.

37.9% → 72.1%Real-robot replay completion

Demos that replay — Touch2Robot (2026)

When demonstrators could see the robot hand's contacts during collection, replay completion jumped from 37.9% to 72.1% — and each usable demo took 18.2 s instead of 58.6 s.

02

Built for teams collecting robot training data

Who it's for

SensePoint is not a general-purpose glove. It is built first for two buyers who feel the missing-contact problem every day.

Primary · Robotics startups

Embodied AI & dexterous-hand teams

You are training manipulation policies and your demos fail on contact, not vision. SensePoint adds pressure, bend and orientation in sync with video — so replay and training use the same signal your robot hand will need.

Primary · Data-collection companies

Demonstration data at scale

You sell or operate human demonstration pipelines. A thin, durable, wireless glove your operators can wear for full sessions — with CSV and raw-stream export that drops into existing labelling and training stacks.

Also used for

Teleoperation & hand R&D

Teleoperation, dexterous-hand validation, ergonomics and assembly QA — anywhere contact force is the variable you cannot currently measure.

Honest fit check

Not a force-feedback or mocap replacement

SensePoint measures contact; it does not track full-body pose and does not push back. If you already own mocap gloves, this is the missing channel — not a replacement. We will tell you on the demo call if it is not a fit.

Data format

Pressure streams as a 16 × 16 array with IMU quaternions over an open serial protocol — read it directly, no black box.

Built to be abused

Z-fold, crumple, and 200,000-impact tested at 3 MPa. The fabric springs back — no recalibration ritual before a session.

Capture software

  • Live pressure maps — 2D, 3D, and matrix views of the full array
  • Record, store, replay — review a grasp frame by frame after the session
  • CSV export — raw data out in one step, ready for your training stack
  • Zoned analysis — box-select regions, track center of pressure, swap in your robot's 3D model
  • English / 中文 UI — Windows 8+ and macOS
  • Pairs with motion capture — SensePoint adds the contact channel that mocap gloves (Manus-class) don't measure

Beyond data capture

The same glove is also used for teleoperation, dexterous-hand R&D, rehabilitation, ergonomics and assembly QA, prosthetics research, and surgical training.

One honest boundary: SensePoint measures force; it doesn't push back. For VR force feedback you need a different, heavier device — we'll tell you so on a call.

07

Open where it helps you. Closed where it protects the product.

Open-core approach

Our recommendation — and our plan — is hybrid: open the integration layer so your team and the community can build on SensePoint without waiting for us, and keep the sensing core closed so quality and calibration stay accountable.

Open

SDK, protocol & examples

Serial protocol, 16 × 16 data format, CSV structure and integration examples are documented and readable — no black box. This is how a small team earns ecosystem iteration without giving away the product.

Closed

Sensing design & calibration

Sensor construction, firmware core and factory calibration stay proprietary. That protects data quality, warranty and the future dataset business — and it is why the public datasheet below withholds core detail.

09

Questions, answered

FAQ
Does the glove provide force feedback?
No — SensePoint is sensing-only: contact pressure, finger bend, hand orientation. No actuators is exactly why it weighs 35.4 g and stays under 2.33 mm thin.
Can I read the raw data myself?
Yes. The serial protocol is open — pressure as a 16 × 16 array (8-bit per point) with IMU quaternions alongside, plus CSV export from the capture software. Need a specific format or sync signal? Put it in the quote request.
Bluetooth or wired — which should I use?
Both stream at 100 Hz. Bluetooth gives you free, natural demonstrations (about 3.75 hours per charge, ~1 week standby). USB serial powers the glove from the host for all-day capture stations and fixed rigs. Most data programs use Bluetooth for collection and USB on the bench.
How does this work with motion-capture gloves?
They measure different things and are usually combined: mocap gloves (Manus-class) track finger pose; SensePoint measures contact. Touch2Robot's rig used exactly that pairing. If you already own mocap, SensePoint is the missing channel, not a replacement.
Can I order a custom size or a robot-hand version?
Not at this time. Customisation is a future option — today SensePoint is sold in standard sizes and geometry only, so we can support quality and delivery properly. Tell us on a demo call what geometry you need and we will log it for the roadmap.
What about calibration and durability?
The fabric is Z-fold and crumple tested, rated for 200,000 impacts at 3 MPa, and springs back without a recalibration ritual. Every glove passes a factory check on every sensing point (response and overflow thresholds) plus a five-finger linearity test before it ships.
How is it priced?
Hardware starts at US $3,000+ per glove. Pair and multi-unit pricing, plus any data services, are quoted with a breakdown after a short demo call — so the number reflects your pipeline, not a generic list. No sales-call ambush.
When can I get one, and where does it ship from?
First stock arrives in Toronto at the end of November 2026 and ships from Canada. Exact lead time for your quantity is confirmed on the demo call — we do not promise a date we cannot hold.
What are the data services — and can I buy datasets?
Data services are a paid add-on for glove owners: collection-program setup, formatting and delivery support for your training stack, quoted per program. Licensed tactile datasets are in development and not on sale yet — discuss early partnerships on a demo call.
